about: Real, openly licensed clinical images shown beside the synthetic ones. Only CC0 / public domain / CC BY / MIT / Apache-2.0 material is accepted; NC, ND, share-alike-only, research-only or unclear sources are rejected. Teaching use only; not diagnostic.

items.title: Portable AP film, ventilated patient
items.caption: Endotracheal tube in the trachea, ECG leads and lines; patchy airspace opacities in both lungs (COVID-19 pneumonia) — the pattern the ARDS lesson draws.
look: Lines and leads crossing the film
items.author: Institute for Diagnostic and Interventional Radiology, Hannover Medical School (MHH), Germany
items.source: COVID-19 Image Repository — https://github.com/ml-workgroup/covid-19-image-repository (copy retrieved from https://github.com/ieee8023/covid-chestxray-dataset, images/<id>.jpg)
items.changes: Converted to greyscale JPEG, downscaled to 1000 px.

items.title: Portable AP film, severe bilateral disease
items.caption: Dense opacities in both lungs with many tubes, lines and leads over the chest — typical of a sick ICU patient; the lines are not lung disease.
look: Many external lines — follow each one
Borders of heart and diaphragm blurred
items.author: Institute for Diagnostic and Interventional Radiology, Hannover Medical School (MHH), Germany
items.source: COVID-19 Image Repository — https://github.com/ml-workgroup/covid-19-image-repository (copy retrieved from https://github.com/ieee8023/covid-chestxray-dataset, images/<id>.jpg)
items.changes: Converted to greyscale JPEG, downscaled to 1000 px.

items.title: Bedside film, lungs largely clear
items.caption: A bedside ("Bettaufnahme") film with largely clear lungs and an implanted port in the left upper chest — a baseline to compare against.
look: Port catheter from the left chest wall
items.author: Institute for Diagnostic and Interventional Radiology, Hannover Medical School (MHH), Germany
items.source: COVID-19 Image Repository — https://github.com/ml-workgroup/covid-19-image-repository (copy retrieved from https://github.com/ieee8023/covid-chestxray-dataset, images/<id>.jpg)
items.changes: Converted to greyscale JPEG, downscaled to 1000 px.

items.title: A-lines: aerated lung
items.caption: Longitudinal anterior chest scan in aerated lung: horizontal repeats of the pleural line (A-lines). Faint in this clip.
items.author: Ana Luisa Silveira Vieira, José Muniz Pazeli Júnior, Marcus Gomes Bastos
items.source: “Role of point-of-care ultrasound during the COVID-19 pandemic: our recommendations in the management of dialytic patients”, The Ultrasound Journal 12:30 (2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13089-020-00177-4 (clip via https://github.com/jannisborn/covid19_ultrasound)
items.changes: Cropped (dataset), first 3.5 s re-encoded to H.264 480 px, contrast and brightness increased; poster frame at 1.2 s.

items.title: B-lines
items.caption: Right lateral chest in COVID-19 pneumonia: vertical bright B-lines from the pleural line to the bottom of the screen, alternating with A-lines, and a thickened pleura.
look: They reach the bottom of the screen
items.author: Giovanni Volpicelli, Luna Gargani
items.source: “Sonographic signs and patterns of COVID-19 pneumonia”, The Ultrasound Journal 12:22 (2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13089-020-00171-w (clip via https://github.com/jannisborn/covid19_ultrasound)
items.changes: Cropped (dataset), first 3.5 s re-encoded to H.264 480 px; poster frame at 1.2 s.

items.title: White lung: confluent B-lines
items.caption: H1N1 pneumonia, lateral mid-chest: confluent B-lines ("white lung") with superficial consolidation and a thickened pleural line.
items.author: Americo Testa, Gino Soldati, Roberto Copetti, Rosangela Giannuzzi, Grazia Portale, Nicolò Gentiloni-Silveri
items.source: “Early recognition of the 2009 pandemic influenza A (H1N1) pneumonia by chest ultrasound”, Critical Care 16:R30 (2012), https://doi.org/10.1186/cc11201 (clip via https://github.com/jannisborn/covid19_ultrasound)
items.changes: Cropped (dataset), first 3.5 s re-encoded to H.264 480 px; poster frame at 1.2 s.
